title: Purity of Heart and the Ropes of Sin
english: Fixing the heart upon this, he considers it pure, and through not staring intensely at it, he may be shown mercy according to the word of his teaching, if the spoken words are such. Is the one seeing the face of God. Jesus teach you, saying, 'Blessed    are the pure in heart, for they shall see God' (Matt 5:8).

And what are the ropes, namely the evil thoughts and the evil powers that subvert these, which they undertake to cast down the standing against God? But the zeal of those surrounding the righteous with ropes is unceasing, those who with rapid zeal remember the law. The same circumstances occurring to the righteous through the sinners can also be ropes for them; but the righteous, bearing these patiently, does not forget the law of God. And those who entangle ropes into sin through deceptive words; but if one remains sober, he does not forget the law of God (Ps 118:63).

Let us also consider the friend and companion, which says the Preacher, 'that if he falls, the one is to raise his companion' (Eccl 4:9-10). He does not at any time intend to say, 'I am a friend and companion to all who fear God and keep his commandments,' while he himself fears him and keeps his commandments.

If there is not kindness and severity concerning God according to the apostle, the kindness becomes for those standing in faith, but the severity for those having fallen away from it. Since the saint was confirmed in faith, 'Kindness, O God, you have done with your servant,' he says; but he says, wanting to present not through destruction the kindness of God with someone, but with the one serving him, whomsoever he may be. And 'according to your word' approaching implies that the kindness of the Lord becomes with someone with word and a logical cause. Therefore, he who wishes to know the logical and wise part of it, deserves no other teacher to be with him concerning it, so that he may learn with it both instruction and knowledge: instruction indeed the ethical, and knowledge the intellectual virtue of good things. And in Proverbs, 'Get instruction and not silver, and knowledge rather than tested gold' (Prov 4:7).
practical and theoretical benefit

title: Resurrection and the Spiritual Life
english: Regarding the mediator, the prophet says to him that the law of the divine mouth is good above all the pleasures of the world, which he showed through thousands of gold and silver. For contemplation, it must be said that silver stands for the word, and gold stands for the mind; for many thousands of such silver and gold are found in those who philosophize about the things of the world and heresies. Above all these things, the law of the mouth of God is good to the lover of the wisdom and truth of God, for those who attend to it alone receive the proper benefit.

Psalm 118:74: 'Understand and not thus: those fearing God are perfect, they not lacking anything; and such are found good, they do not lack fear.' Therefore they desire all to progress and to have benefit, and they rejoice over those things pleasing to God, imitating those in heaven who rejoice over the benefit of the penitents. It is also possible to take the inferior [understanding] regarding 'they shall be glad,' as it says: 'They shall see and be glad,' where the mind of the things said is such. 'Hoping in your words, I desire to become completely [one with you], I act and think according to your instruction'; and those fearing lest they fall into the punishment following the judgment which pursues sinners, they avoid evil. If those fearing you in this way are not able to see me, they shall be glad, no longer avoiding sins out of grief and necessity, but with zeal to take them up, hoping also themselves in your words.

Psalm 118:77a: Since the mercies of God are said to be not only here but also in many other places, one must watch lest the only-begotten and the Holy Spirit, the providers of life, are not [seen as] the mercies of God. And Father is said, according to the apostle's philosophy of the mercies.
Psalm 118:78a: Of a great man, he says: 'Unjustly I have transgressed against me.'

Psalm 118:81: 'My soul fails for the salvation of God, but the end of faith shall bring salvation'; for there remains no soul, setting aside the state through which the soul used to exist, but desiring the salvation of God and continuing in hope, the spirit and mind becoming [one] with his word. For the name of the soul does not declare its essence, but the relationship toward the communion of the body. But if it might pass over to incorporeal life and be uncorrupted...

Receiving bread and a spiritual body from a resurrection, the body which was formerly joined to it, corruptible and psychic in being possessed by a soul, shall become mind and spirit, leaving behind the divine salvation and being in spirit toward God through Him. And this is to deny oneself; for he who has denied himself will become one thing instead of another, not according to the underlying substance but according to that which makes it, sometimes soul, sometimes mind. For even if the evangelical sayings are exhortations toward martyrdom, they are not to be understood according to the aforementioned mystical word.

The word of God is a spiritual dew (Ps 118:83a), since dew and rain are often called; it cools my unbridled flame from passions and makes my flesh weak, as to bear the death of Jesus in it. Many attempt to interpret the divine writings of the Church and those outside it, both heretics and Jews and Samaritans (Ps 118:85), but not all speak well; for rare is the one possessing the grace from God for this, speaking of many things promised, but living not well and unlawfully. If they say anything, it is wandering and babbling; for a word cannot be vigorous, strong, and salutary in an unlawful soul.

Those pursuing righteousness and the teaching of Christ will healthily speak the aforementioned word (Ps 118:87a), and all the prophets also. And to be accomplished is in the earth, not the common dying, but that which was called into the material existence as earth, to come to an end in order to be done according to it. To live according to the word of God is to live with piety (Ps 118:88), not simply this sensory life. For having obtained this, he will be in well-being, as to guard the testimonies of the mouth of God testified and demonstrated by the word of God, which are in His mouth.

The day remains by Your ordinance (Ps 118:91a), as to circle regularly and uniformly according to the annual cycles, the day not deviating, never having toward night an ordinance of inequality or inequality. title: The Law as Light and the Progression of Knowledge
english: those who followed him
Turn away from evil and do good; for he who turns away from evil from every wicked way restrains his feet, so that having done good, he may guard the words of God (Ps 118:105).

The law is a lamp to those walking in the night before the rising of the sun of righteousness (Ps 118:106); just as the night has passed and the day has approached, they are illuminated not by a lamp but by the sun of the true light, so that it is possible to walk decorously during the day.

And to set [it] here and to define firmly signifies to stand fast, and to swear is not merely to name God, but to set this thing unchangeably and to guard it without transgression, performing the work of an oath by power (Ps 118:124).

Not as if, not having attained the petition, he approaches it again, but as having learned the ordinances of God according to a prior worthiness; as one who is spending time with them, desiring to contemplate them more greatly, he needs and always does this, so that he may reach the goal of their understanding (Ps 118:125).

Since, however, regarding the learning of the ordinances, various things are becoming [different], I will say this also concerning the knowledge of the testimonies: that through progress, their knowledge is always becoming ascended for the one spending time with their comprehension (Ps 118:127).

'Your mouth's law is more precious to me than ten thousands of gold and silver' (Ps 118:127), and 'Take instruction and do not forsake knowledge, which is tested above silver' (Prov 8:10); for wisdom is more excellent than precious stones, and every precious thing is not of equal value to it. Therefore it is also said to companions concerning it to Job: 'The balance of Ethiopia shall not equal it' (Job 28:15). These things are not said by comparison but in relation to the value of men.

He who has come to fulfill the law and all the prophets, making manifest the words contained in them (Ps 118:130), does this by fulfilling the prophecies, and does this by uncovering the law, so that it is seen no longer as letter and shadow but as spiritual. For thus the manifestation of the divine words that has occurred will prove the prophet to be sensible and will enlighten those called from the nations after Israel, who are infants in their weakness and have late or tardy come to a generation from faith.
